cases.purpose: bashio chown applies numeric UID, GID, UID:GID and :GID specs through lchown and rejects missing operands with the usage status.
cases.oracle: Expected values follow the lchown(2) contract and the documented bashio chown semantics; ownership and ctime are read back by an independent python3 lstat observer, with synthetic /etc/passwd and /etc/group bind-mounted in a private user+mount namespace (uid/gid 0 inside is the guest's 2000).
cases.comparison: Candidate output, status and files compared with values derived independently of candidate output.

files.inner.sh:
/usr/bin/mount --bind passwd /etc/passwd && /usr/bin/mount --bind group /etc/group || exit 97
O() { /usr/bin/python3 obs.py "$@"; }
O fifo wait.fifo; exec 7<> wait.fifo
tick() { read -t 0.06 -u 7 || :; }
r() { local l=$1; shift; "$@" 2>err.txt; local rc=$?; local e; e=$(< err.txt)
  printf '%s status=%s' "$l" "$rc"
  case $e in '') printf ' err=none';; *"unknown user"*) printf ' err=unknown-user';; *"unknown group"*) printf ' err=unknown-group';;
    *"Invalid argument"*) printf ' err=EINVAL';; *"needs UID"*) printf ' err=usage';; *) printf ' err=other:%s' "$e";; esac
  printf '\n'; }
